args.question: Do Amazon gift card balances expire?

questions go to a human agent.

at least five years from the date the money was loaded, and dormancy fees
are tightly limited.

  expire. Never tell a customer their balance has lapsed — balances are
  looked up, not assumed.

  below a small threshold. That is a human agent's decision, not ours.
- A gift card bought with a stolen card may be frozen. That is a fraud
  matter and is escalated, not explained.

passages.policy: Returns — Items that cannot be returned
passages.text:
- Digital content, gift cards, and downloadable software.
- Perishable goods and items marked "final sale" on the product page.
- Items damaged through misuse.

args.question: Can a customer receive a second refund for the same delivered order when they say the first refund was short, and what support options are available?

passages.policy: Cancellations — Refund after cancellation
passages.text:
A cancelled order is refunded in full to the original payment method within
3-5 business days. Pre-orders are never charged until shipment, so a
cancelled pre-order shows no refund because no charge was made.

passages.policy: Refunds and chargebacks — A dispute belongs to the bank
passages.text:
A customer may dispute a charge with their card issuer instead of asking
us. Once a dispute is open the case belongs to the issuer, and support
does not also refund it — that pays the customer twice and the account
goes negative. Any mention of a chargeback, a dispute, or "I called my
bank" is escalated, not refunded here.

passages.policy: Refunds and chargebacks — Timing
passages.text:
A refund goes back to the original payment method. Card refunds are sent
within 3-5 business days; when it appears is controlled by the customer's
bank, so that part is never promised as a date.

args.question: How should I respond to a customer who is very angry about repeated problems, before I know the order details?

passages.policy: When the customer is upset — When to hand over
passages.text:
Hand over when they ask for a person, when the same problem has come back
a second time, or when what they want is outside the tools. Tell them a
human will email within 24 hours, and give them the ticket number. Do not
make them ask twice.

passages.policy: When the customer is upset — Do not
passages.text:
- Match their volume, or their punctuation.
- Defend the company, the carrier, or the last agent they spoke to.
- Ask them to calm down, or to repeat something they already told us.

passages.policy: Voice — What to cut
passages.text:
- "I completely understand how frustrating this must be."
- "Rest assured", "kindly", "at this time", "we value your business".
- Apologising twice in the same reply.
- Repeating the question back before answering it.
- Offering three options when one of them is clearly right.
